# Jubilees Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Watchers; Nephilim; The Flood Decreed

---

**5:1** And it came to pass when the children of men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of God saw them on a certain year of this jubilee, that they were beautiful to look upon; and they took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare unto them sons and they were giants.

**5:2** And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth — all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men was thus evil continually.

**5:3** And God looked upon the earth, and behold it was corrupt, and all flesh had corrupted its orders, and all that were upon the earth had wrought all manner of evil before his eyes.

**5:4** And he said that he would destroy man and all flesh upon the face of the earth which he had created.

**5:5** But Noah found grace before the eyes of the LORD.

**5:6** And against the angels whom he had sent upon the earth, he was exceedingly wroth, and he gave commandment to root them out of all their dominion, and he bade us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold they are bound in the midst of them, and are kept separate.

**5:7** And against their sons also was he exceedingly wroth, for they had slain each other with the sword, and they had been swallowed up in wickedness.

**5:8** And he sent the sword amongst them that each should slay his neighbor, and they began to slay each other till they all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.

**5:9** And their fathers also witnessed it, and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment is executed on all those who have corrupted their ways and their works before the LORD.

**5:10** And he destroyed all from their places, and there was not left one of them whom he did not judge according to all their wickedness.

**5:11** And he made for all his works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever, but should be all righteous each in his kind always.

**5:12** And the judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets in righteousness — even the judgment of all who depart from the path which is ordained for them to walk in; and if they walk not therein, judgment is written down for every creature and for every kind.

**5:13** And there is nothing in heaven or on earth or in light or in darkness or in the depths of the abyss or in the deep darkness, in all your dwelling places, that is not judged and that is not written on the heavenly tablets.

**5:14** And he said: "Let my spirit not forever abide in man, for they are flesh, and their days shall be one hundred and twenty years."

**5:15** And he sent his sword into their midst that each might slay his neighbor, and they began to slay each other till they all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.

**5:16** And their fathers witnessed and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment is executed on all those who have corrupted their ways and their works before the LORD.

**5:17** And he destroyed all their places, and there was not left one of them whom he did not judge according to all their wickedness.

**5:18** And he made for all his works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever, but should be all righteous each in his kind always.

**5:19** And the judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets in righteousness.

**5:20** And Noah made an ark in all of these things in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week in the fifth year.

**5:21** And he entered in the sixth year thereof, and he shut its doors in the seventh month in the seventeenth day in the second month of the first year of the twenty-eighth jubilee, and the LORD opened seven flood-gates of heaven and the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths.

**5:22** And the flood-gates began to pour down water from the heaven forty days and forty nights, and the fountains of the deep also sent up waters, until the whole world was full of water.

**5:23** And the waters increased upon the face of the earth: and they covered all the high mountains, and all that was under the heaven was covered with waters until fifteen cubits above the highest mountains were covered by the waters.

**5:24** And the ark was lifted up above the earth, and it moved upon the face of the waters.

**5:25** And the water prevailed on the face of the earth five months — one hundred and fifty days.

**5:26** And the ark went and rested on the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.

**5:27** And in the fourth month the fountains of the great deep were closed and the flood-gates of heaven were restrained; and on the new moon of the seventh month all the mouths of the abysses of the earth were opened, and the water began to descend into the deep below.

**5:28** And in the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains were seen, and Noah was glad.

**5:29** And after forty days Noah opened the window of the ark, and he sent forth a raven to see if the waters had abated; but it went and returned, for the waters were still upon the face of the whole earth.

**5:30** And he waited yet other seven days, and sent forth a dove to see if the waters had abated from off the face of the earth, but it found no resting place for the sole of its foot and returned to him.

**5:31** And he waited yet other seven days, and sent forth a dove; and the dove returned with a branch of olive — leaves in its mouth — and Noah knew that the waters had abated from off the earth.

**5:32** And on the first day of the first month of the year he opened the covering of the ark, and looked, and behold the face of the earth was dry.

**5:33** And in the twenty-eighth jubilee Noah opened the ark, and sent forth from it beasts and cattle, and birds, and every moving thing.

---
*EMET notes: Jubilees' Watchers narrative (vv.1-19) telescopes Gen 6 with the 1 Enoch tradition: angels took wives, begat giants, caused universal corruption. Judgment on the giants (v.8): they kill each other by the sword. Angels bound "in the depths of the earth" (v.9). V.14 quotes Gen 6:3 within Jubilees' framework. Noah's ark rests on "Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat" (v.26) — the Jubilees-specific name for the peak.*
